title: SnFe 2 O 4 –rGO heterojunction for visible light driven photocatalytic degradation of methylene blue: a combined experimental and theoretical study
content: The widespread use of methylene blue (MB) in industrial processes and its subsequent release into aquatic environments necessitate effective removal strategies. In this study, a novel composite material was synthesized via co-precipitation by integrating tin–iron oxide (SnFe2O4) with reduced graphene oxide (rGO) to enhance the photodegradation of MB under visible light. The incorporation of rGO plays a crucial role in improving the photocatalytic performance by providing a conductive pathway for efficient electron transport, facilitating charge separation, and suppressing electron–hole recombination. The composite achieved a maximum removal efficiency of 60–70% for MB under optimal conditions. This enhancement is attributed to improved charge transport and reduced energy loss at the interface of the composite components. Computational analyses indicated that the SnFe2O4–rGO composite exhibits superior visible light absorption and electrical conductivity compared to pristine SnFe2O4. These findings demonstrate that the SnFe2O4–rGO composite is a safe and effective material for the removal of methylene blue and related contaminants from water.
